newsitem.title: GREECE: OLYMPIC AVIATION TO CUT FLIGHTS TO ISLANDS.
newsitem.headline: OLYMPIC AVIATION TO CUT FLIGHTS TO ISLANDS.

text.p: Olympic Aviation, a subsidiary of Greece's state carrier Olympic Airways, which serves popular holiday islands is expected to reduce its flights for the next two weeks after a "go-slow" action by the company's mechanics.

The state-run Athens News Agency (ANA) said on Monday that at least 19 scheduled flights were cancelled and many more delayed, stranding hundreds of air travelers to the islands -- many of them foreign tourists.
Popular island destinations like Paros, Mykonos, Santorini, Skiathos, Zakynthos, Milos and Chios would be served by less than normal flights for the next two weeks.
The mechanics, who demand the employment of more staff, refused to work overtime saying that during the busy summer season they are forced to work an average of five hours overtime per day.
Tourism minister Vasso Papandreou made a plea to the mechanics to stop their action saying it threatened to seriously damage the tourist season.

Olympic Aviation's board was holding an all-day emergency meeting to deal with the situation but airport officials said more delays and flight cancellations were expected later in the day and on Tuesday.
